turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. Based on the news, may nakita po kami nun.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy Tulfo
turns.text: When was that? When did that happen?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: 2024 yata, yung 75 PNP personnel from BPSPG, Sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy Tulfo
turns.text: Was that before the utterance of PPSPG sa Prescon or after?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Before, Sir. Before? I think that's before, Sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy Tulfo
turns.text: So would it be possible na because of that, nakapag-isip siya na mayroon threat against her life?

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy Tulfo
turns.text: iyong security niya being pulled out, and walang binigay na reason kung bakit. Kaya maaaring iniisip niya na, well, medyo, sabi nga, sakali na praning—

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Very much possible, sir. Opo.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy Tulfo
turns.text: But hindi ninyo ba inimbestigahan bakit na-pull out iyong security details niya?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: May nakita kami doon sa November 26 na video. Nalimutan ko lang iyong timestamp niya. May sinasabi siyang issue sa security niya. Doon nga sa BPSPG, parang from military attached unit, ginawang under na ng Presidential Security Command. I'm not familiar with that.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy Tulfo
turns.text: Sino pong nag-cause ng pull out? Sino pong nag-utos? Saan galing yung utos?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Atty. Dico Hu, siya masyado. Pero I think part ng reorganization, Your Honor, ng PSG if I'm not mistaken.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy Tulfo
turns.text: Part ng reorganization. So, ilan po yung napulo? 75?

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy Tulfo
turns.text: Hindi ko

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: pa alam kung yan yun. Ang sinasabi ko po, Your Honor, yung dating BPSPG is under ng attached unit ng Armed Forces of the Philippines, kung di ako nagkakamali. And then, inilagay na siya sa ilalim ng…

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Presidential Security Command. Yun po yung sinabi ng Vice Presidente during November 26 na security threat dahil doon sa event na yon. Yun po yung tinignan namin. Tinignan din namin yan. Pati nga yung 75 personnel. Kaya lang again, hindi po siya sufficient na mag-establish ng apparent violation of any criminal offense. Kasi nga, para siyang normal na function ng

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy Tulfo
turns.text: agencies and departments. Yeah, Mr. Huertas, yung sa akin na kasi yung pag-pull out ba ng security, was it sudden? Did it, I mean, ano yung naging dahilan? At kanino galing yung order para i-pull out yung ilang numbers of security details niya, particularly PNP? And then sabi nyo nga, yung sa PSG, nabawasan din ba? Base sa inyong investigation, bakit nga po nangyari yun?

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy Tulfo
turns.text: Agencies and Departments Anong nag-trigger noon?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Opo, iyong sa 75, ang naalala ko po sa news, parang inilipat ho sila, Your Honor, sa Manila kasi merong issue na kailangan nilang i-augment dahil may peace-and-order issue sa Manila. So iyon ang nakita kong nasa news na ginawa ng PNP, o reason ng PNP.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: ng PNP bakit mayroong ganoong pullout. Then, noong nakita ho namin ilan na lang iyong natira sa Vice President, noong chineck ho namin iyong news, iyong per record ng COA, if I'm not mistaken, meron pa siyang 335 na security personnel.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy Tulfo
turns.text: Ah, so marami pang naiwan?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yes po, Your Honor. In fact, kung hindi ako nagkakamali, narinig ko po iyong sinabi ni Honorable Boying Remulla na

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yung bilang na yan, mas marami pa doon sa bilang ng mga security personnel ng Presidente. So

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: nakita ko namin na hindi sa sufficient para maging valid basis ng investigation. Hindi ko katulad dito sa threat against the president na apparent po yung utterances na nangyayari.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy Tulfo
turns.text: Okay, dalawang katulungan na lamang, Mr. Witness. So base sa inyong investigasyon at karanasan, Ilan ba dapat ang security detail ng isang vice president?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Sorry po, Your Honor. Wala po akong idea kung ilan po dapat. Last

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy Tulfo
turns.text: na lamang. So nung na-pull out yung ilan sa mga security personnel niya, sabi niyo nga 75, right? PNP and then meron pa ating sa PSG. Nagreklamo ba siya?

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy Tulfo
turns.text: Sa inyong pagkakaalam?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Doon sa November 26, Your Honor, I think ang isa sa

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: issue niya na may threat sa security is yung paglipat ng BBSPG. From attached unit ng AFP na maging under siya ng Presidential Security Command. Yun po yung narinig namin. Pero yun dito sa 75 personnel, insofar as I'm concerned, wala akong nakita sa reports, sa news, sa social media na nagreklamo siya na nawala yung 75. Pero baka malihaw ako, baka mayroon akong hindi nakita. Pero insofar as I'm concerned, Wala akong nakita sa news na nagreklamo siya doon sa 75 transfer ng PNP personnel from BPSPG dinala doon sa Manila, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy Tulfo
turns.text: At hindi na siya nag-request ng augmentation o dagdag doon sa mga nawala na security detail?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Mukhang hindi na po, Your Honor. Wala akong kaming nalaman kung may nirequest ba siyang dagdag.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy Tulfo
turns.text: So is it possible na dahil doon sa pag-pull out ng security details, nasabi ko na kanina, tonight, tanong ko na again one more time, na...

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy Tulfo
turns.text: Yun yun probably ang tinitingnan na reasons ng mga sumusuporta sa kanya, siya or anybody sa circle niya na eto na siguro yun.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Tama po kayo, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Raffy Tulfo
turns.text: Thank you.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Senator Judge Alan Caetano, you have two minutes, sir. You may proceed when you're ready.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Sir, Presiding Officer, Dear Colleagues, susundahan ko lang po yung kay Sen. Riza, Sen. Judge Riza, Sen. Judge J.V. at yung ibang nagtanong sa admission against interest. You stated this already but just for the record, you viewed the whole video, right? The whole 2-hour video.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: The November 23, sir. Yes. Yeah, isang beses, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Isang bes lang?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Okay. And how many times there has the vice president made admissions against her interest?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: No, sir. Ang tinutukoy ko pong admissions against interest doon sa November 26, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: No. Sabi mo yung November 23 din na ayaw ng defense gamitin contracted. So yung kinausap is also an admission against her interest, di ba?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Di, Sir. Ang sinasabi ko po ang admissions against interest, yung November 26 video po, Sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Na sinasabi niyang totoo yun at hindi niya sinasabi? Yes, Sir. Okay.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: So, doon sa November 23, may nakita ka doon na admissions against interest?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: In so far as I'm concerned, na nireiterate niya. Hindi,

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: not nireiterate. Siguro para malinaw. In your mind, as a lawyer or as an NBI agent, what is an admission against interest?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Iyon nga po iyong in-explain ko kanina. Ito po iyong isang bagay na ginawa ng isang tao—hindi ginawa, sinabi. Kasi it's an admission. Sinabi ng isang tao na ikakasira niya.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: But then, instead of denying na sinabi niya yun, In-admit pa niya ito o nire-iterate niya? Okay.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Very clear yan. And you and Agent John Mark Kalilong said that the basis of the investigation was the November 23 video. The basis sa inyong affidavit of investigation sa nag-file ng kaso is certain portions of the November 23 video.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: As well

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: as other evidence. Okay. Sa November 23, ilan ang admission niya against interest?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Ang sinasabi ko pong admission against interest yung

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: November 26. This is a new question. If you evaluated well the November 23 video,

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Is there any circumstance in that video that you believe that the Vice President made admissions against her interest?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Plain ho yung utterance niya doon, Your Honor. Yung nakita lang namin yung utterances niya. Insofar as I'm concerned, yung admission against interest nangyayari nung November 26.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Mr. Witness, sagutin ninyo na lang ako. Lahat ng admissions are utterances?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Okay? Admissions is verbal. Di ba? Hindi ito yung parang admission sa court. Pwede mo i-admit yung documentary evidence, pwede yung object evidence, pwede yung statements. When we talk about admissions against interest, especially in context of what we're talking about, may statement na laban sa interest niya.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: So tinatanong ko dun sa buong video, meron ka bang nakita? Wala. Yes or no lang yun. Meron or wala? O meron at wala, hindi yes or no?

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Kayo nag-evaluate nun eh. Meron o wala? Admissions against her interest?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yes, sir. The fact na inuttered niya yun. Oh,

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: which one nga? So, meron ilan at ano yun? A little bit leeway, Mr. Presiding Officer, kasi hindi natukoy masyado yung tanong.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Senators, judge, may proceed.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: So, which statement that? That one you're mentioning now. So, yung sagot mo, meron.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Ang understanding ko, sir, nung sinabi ko yan, I'm referring to the November 26, 2024.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Mr. Witness, paulit-ulit tayo.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Burahin mo na yung pinag-uusapan natin you're referring to. I'm asking you a direct question.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Sa November 23, meron o wala bang statements that you would consider, in your professional opinion as a lawyer and as an NBI agent in charge of investigating this, admissions against interest?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Ang tinutukoy ko lang po again, Your Honor, yung 23.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Wala po yung 23. I'm sorry. I don't care, Mr. Presiding Officer, kung anong tinutukoy mo. I'm asking you a direct question. November 23, video. Meron o wala siyang admissions against your interest doon?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Atty. Lotoc, yes, no, I do not know, I do not remember. We're referring to November 23, not 26.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yeah, I do not know, sir. Ang nare-refer ko na...

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Don't tell me na. So you do not know. Okay. When she said, kung papatayin ako, may kausap na ako, patayin niyo yung tatlo, is that an admission against interest? Yes or no?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Based on that utterances, sir, yes. I think so.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Yes. O, kakasabi mo lang kanina, 'I don't know.' Ngayon, yes. O ano pa? Ano pa sa video na iyon na admission against interest? Meron o wala? Or, 'I don't know'?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Iyong utterances na iyon, sir. Sir—

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: bukod nga dun.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: To me, sir, yung utterances na yun, that's admission against interest?

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Sir, klaro na yun. Tinanong ka na ng presiding officer, sagot mo, I don't know. Tinanong kita ng diretsyo, nasa video, biglang you know, biglang sasabihin mo na yun, utterance na yun. So ang tanong ko na ngayon, bukod dun, aside from that.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Sir, ulitin ko po yung sagot ko. No,

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: you don't need to answer.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: No, I'm asking you, aside from the utterance, the statement, na kung papatayin nila ako, patayin sila. Is there any other utterance during in that video that you would consider admission against interest? In so far as I

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: remember, wala na po yun.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Wala na. Okay. When the vice president said, yung pinamigay sa DepEd, isn't that an admission against our interest kung may pinamigay?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Siya po yung namigay, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Ikaw ang nanood ng video. Ikaw ang nag-evaluate. Ako pa magsasabi sa'yo kung ano laman ng video? Akala ko ba tinignan niyo ng mabuti yung video? Bakit hindi mo alam yung laman ng video?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: E. D. S. W. Sir, pwede ko pong tingnan yung sinasabi n

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: 'yo? So you do not know what the alaman ng video?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Again, tinignan ko po ang video one time. Ang nag-review po ng video, yung agent on case.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Yes, but you're the agent in charge. And you're the one who filed the affidavit. Okay, next question. Nung sinabing mag-people power, tapos ang sinabi niya hindi yun yung solusyon. Kung nag-people power, sino magiging presidente? Kung nag-people power at mawawala ang Pangulong Marcos, sino magiging presidente?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Siya, sir. So

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: hindi ba admission against her interest din? Siguro sa interest niya maging presidente. Pero ang sinabi niya, wag.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: I think so, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Okay. So I mentioned three. So my next question. When you have an admission against interest, do you take the whole admission or you can cut it up into parts?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Again, Your Honor, iyong— If

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: my admission against interest is one sentence or one paragraph or three sentences, can you take one sentence and say yun lang yung admission and the two other sentences are not? I think

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: it should be the whole, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: The whole sentence. So the whole sentence niya, nung sinabi niyang kung papatayin ako, is pinagbibintangan niya yung tatlo na papatayin siya. So if you say it's an admission against interest and you believe it, you also have to believe na papatayin siya nung tatlo. The same thing, if you're going to say na namudmud siya sa DepEd, ang sinabi niya galing sa First Lady yung pera. So you're also going to have to believe that. So if you're going to believe her, na yung ibang sinabi ay seditious, eh ngayon sinabi nga niya hindi solusyon ng people power. So as the evaluator, Bakit hindi consistent yung evaluation niyo nung video?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: No, I think insofar as people power is concerned, I think sinabi niya yata na, yes ma'am, natutuwa ako dun sa ginagawa niyo. Hindi.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Pwede ko pong ulitin. Let the

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: record speak for itself. It's on page 26. Same paragraph nung sinabi niya ang papatayan. But having said that, last question.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Bakit sa cybercrime ni-refer? Bakit hindi sa anti-terrorism or sinabi mo meron intel group? Bakit sa cyber crime?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Your Honor, may cyber aspect po kasi yung violation.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Okay. What are the aspects of the alleged threat? One is the cyber crime grave threat. The other one is a possible assassination threat, right?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: No, Your Honor. Yung sinasabi kong may cyber aspect, the utterance was made through...

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Through cyber. And the utterance... In accordance with you, constitute grade threat.

turns.speaker: Sen. Panfilo M. Lacson
turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: But if she meant it, and if it is true, and if it is accurate, it's also an assassination plot, isn't it?

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Kung totoo yung utterance niya, napapapatay kita, may kausap na ako, hindi ba assassination plot yun?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Maybe, sir. Yes.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Hindi maybe. NBI kayo, kayo nag-ano eh. May nagsabi sa presidente, papatayin kita. How much plain can that be as an assassination plot?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: That's why, sir, may validation process.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: That's why

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: may validation. Kaya yung tanong ko. Ano ba mas mabigat? Yung assassination plot o yung cyber aspect?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: No, Your Honor. No,

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: no. Diretso ang tanong. Hindi no, no, no. Anong mas mabigat? It's a

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: direct question. If you were NBI director now or whatever, you were PNP chief, dalawang iniimbestigahan mo, yung cyber aspect na pwedeng cyber libel, pwedeng grave threat, at yung assassination plot, ano mas mabigat sa dalawa? Ano yung pra-prioritize mo?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Your Honor, yung cyber aspect, based on the law, mag-a-add siya ng one degree higher.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: So, magde-debate tayo kung anong higher: papabayaan mong mapatay ang Presidente?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: winding up.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: The point I want to make, Mr. President, is whether I was the PSC, the Executive Secretary, NBI, or an ordinary citizen, my first concern is wag mapatay ang presidente.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: But instead of the NBI director taking it upon himself, giving it to the anti-terrorists or to the intelligence, sa cybercrime binigay.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Your Honor, again, uulitin ko, yung utterances was made through information and communication technology. Kaya may jurisdiction also.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: I hope if

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: anyone of my colleagues here become president, magbago yung attitude ng NBI. Mas importante pala cyber kaso sa buhay ng presidente. Not necessarily, Your Honor. Thank

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: you, Mr. President.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Noted. Council correspondent is recognized for his recross, if any.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Just a few points, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: You may proceed, sir, when you're ready.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: So, during your testimony, you mentioned that an unsigned document is a mere scrap of paper.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. But you also said on redirect that the lack of signature is a typographical error.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: No. Yung typographical error, based sa tanong sa akin kanina ng abogado, yung misspelling, yung mali yung...

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Docket number, kung mali man iyon.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yun, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Atty. Amando Virgil D. Ligutan
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Now, you mentioned on redirect also about the November 26, 2024 presscon, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: So after that presscon, did you interview VP Sara?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: No, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: And despite not having interviewed her, You made findings on her mental state.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: No? Findings ng mental state, sir? What do you mean by that?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: My question is, despite not having the chance to interview VP Sara, nevertheless, you included in your investigation or findings about her mental state.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Based on the series of events, Your Honor, as I have said, State of mind can be shown through the overt acts, Your Honor. Okay.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: So, you were also asked about persistence, correct?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Now, the subject video was on November 23, 2024, correct? Yes, sir. But to demonstrate persistence, you referred to a presscon on October 18, 2024.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: No, sir. To demonstrate persistence, yung nature ng atirances niya, Ulitin ko siya, in-explain ko muna, the nature of the instruction was persistent because of the fact na ang sabi niya, wag kang tumigil hanggat hindi mo sila mapapatay. And then, i-reiterate niya ito noong November 26. Now, as to consistency patterns at persistence pagdating sa galit niya sa presidente, yung October 18 may kinalaman kasi ang unang sinabi niya doon,

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Valang. Kinukonsider akong number one. Hanggang number two lang yung Pilipinas na to. Then pangalawa, I imagine myself cutting his head.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Then kinumpara namin siya nung November 23. Already satisfied with

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: the answer.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Consistent po yung...

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: What was that, counsel, for responding?

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: We are already satisfied. No need to

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: elaborate. I think already answered. Yes.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Alright. Last two questions. So you said that the February 14, 2025 DOJ certification found your investigation or the case that you filed sufficient?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Based on the certification, the DOJ stated that you have complied all the elements of the crime charge. So

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: this DOJ evaluation, does this amount to a final verdict?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Ang maliwanag hudon for purposes of preliminary investigation. Wala akong sinabing na final verdict.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: So, you also mentioned the concept of open-source investigation. Does this include internet browsing?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: So you Google search? Kasama ba iyon?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Yes, sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Google search mga news articles, websites, videos, correct? Yes, sir. Including mga YouTube videos? Yes, sir. Alright. I'll show you a short video and I'll ask one final question.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Kindly show the video, Tek.

turns.speaker: Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte
turns.text: Worry ko lang is yung mga anak ko dahil hindi talaga yan sila sanay na wala ako. Nasanay kasi sila, lumaki kasi sila na

turns.speaker: Vice President Sara Zimmerman Duterte
turns.text: Katabi ko iyan sila sa tulog. Iyan iyong worry ko, iyong aking mga anak. Dahil nawalan sila ng nanay, iyan iyong hindi ko kasi magawa remotely, iyong pagiging nanay. Pero iyong trabaho dito at trabaho diyan sa Pilipinas, kung saan man ako, magawa ko siya remotely.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: So, in the course of your open-source investigation, did you encounter this video?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Hindi ko po na-encounter yan, Sir.

turns.speaker: Atty. Mark C. Vinluan
turns.text: Nothing further, Your Honors.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Before we let go of the witness, the Presiding Officer just has a few points. Number one, to clarify, Atty. Lotoc, sa pagtatanong po ni Senate President Wengat Shalan kanina, sabi niyo po, maliban sa mga salitang binanggit o sinambit na ikalawang Pangulo na may nakausap na siya na gagawa nung kanyang kautosang patayin, diyo mo no, ang tatlong opisyal ng bansa,

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: wala po kayong hawak na ibang ebidensyang may kinausap na nga siya.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: In so far as the cybercrime division is concerned, sir, opo.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Pangalawa po, sabi ninyo po, sa ilang katanungang ipinukol sa inyo, na hindi ninyo alam kung totoo o hindi ang ilang mga sinabi ng Ikalawang Pangulo sa video na napanood po ninyo nang isang beses, iyong mahigit dalawang oras. Sa kabuuan po, ang kaya ninyo lang pong sabihin ay sinabi niya iyon. Pero kung totoo man iyon o hindi, wala po kayo sa lugar para sabihin na totoo nga ba lahat ng mga sinabi niya?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Well, una, since Vice President siya, at base doon sa circumstance na galit na galit siya at nagbabato siya ng mga pagmumura, we believe na totoo iyong mga sinasabi niya, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: And, as an advisement perhaps to the Senator-Judges and the public as well, an admission against interest as mentioned in the Rules is nothing really special. An admission against interest under the Rules is simply an exception to the hearsay rule. Where a person is about to die or is unavailable to testify, his statements against his or her interest may be admitted, testified to by another person—not the way we seem to be giving admission against interest na parang umamin na dahil labag sa interest niya iyon. The Rules are specific, and the purpose also is specific: it is an exception to the hearsay rule. If there are no other points or questions to be raised by any of the Senator-Judges—

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Senator-Judge Padilla is recognized for his intervention.

turns.speaker: Sen. Robinhood “Robin” Padilla
turns.text: Puwede po bang magtanong ulit?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: You have two minutes, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Robinhood “Robin” Padilla
turns.text: Yes, of course, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Robinhood “Robin” Padilla
turns.text: Kanina po nabanggit kanina ng isang senador na meron pong dalawang kaso. Sa panahon ni Pangulong Rodrigo Roa Duterte na inimbestigahan niyo po, isang hundred fifty million, tsaka ano po yung isa? Ang naalala ko, Your Honor, kay MAS yata. Hindi

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: ako may hawak noon, Your Honor, hindi ako ang Cybercrime Division. I think ibang unit ang nanghuli, although ang Cybercrime

turns.speaker: Sen. Robinhood “Robin” Padilla
turns.text: Division yata yung nag-file. Pero hindi ako may hawak noon.

turns.speaker: Sen. Robinhood “Robin” Padilla
turns.text: Hindi po panahon niyo. Pero ano po nangyari doon? Na-dismiss po ba yan? Ang alam ko na-dismiss yata, Sir. Nagsakuha din po ba sila ng masusing investigasyon? Hindi ko po masasagot. Hindi po ako nag-imbestiga, Your Honor. Wala po kayong nabalitaan kung gumawa din sila ng masusing investigasyon?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Again, Your Honor, kung ibang unit po ang nagsagawa

turns.speaker: Sen. Robinhood “Robin” Padilla
turns.text: noon, wala po akong personal knowledge. Opo, opo. Kasi po doon malinaw eh na mayroong involved na pera. Kasi alam niyo matagal din po ako nakulong. Tatlong taon din po ako sa kulungan. Marami po ako nakasama dyan ng mga hired killers.

turns.speaker: Sen. Robinhood “Robin” Padilla
turns.text: Katunayan, pati po hindi hired killers, nakasama ko din po dyan. Sila Tihanki. Katunayan, excuse po sa aking seatmate, madami po talaga. Pag-usapin po kasi ng pera, talagang may threat. Pero sa tingin po ba niyo yung... Ang mga nangyari noong November 23, birthday ko pa po yun.

turns.speaker: Sen. Robinhood “Robin” Padilla
turns.text: Sa tingin niyo po ba, walang involved na kahit anong pera dito? Walang kahit anong ano? Threat pa rin po ba yun sa palagay ninyo? Kasi ang hired killer, pera-pera po yan.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Based on our findings, great threat, Your Honor, and inciting position.

turns.speaker: Sen. Robinhood “Robin” Padilla
turns.text: Meron po ba? Inciting? Okay. Maganda pong pag-usapan yan. Doon po ba, pagkatapos po ba nung November 23 na mga sinabi ng ating vicepresidente, meron po bang ginawa ang ating mga taong bayan para maging inciting for sedition? Nagbunga po ba ito?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Your Honor, ulitin ko po yung sakot ko. In the case of people versus nabong, hindi ho necessary.

turns.speaker: Sen. Robinhood “Robin” Padilla
turns.text: Pakisagot na lang po kung yes or no. Kung meron po bang naganap na pag... Kilos ang mga tao.

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: In so far as yung Seditious Act, wala kaming nakita, sir.

turns.speaker: Sen. Robinhood “Robin” Padilla
turns.text: Wala po. Opo. Meron pa pong isang tanong. Doon po ba sa mga naganap na maraming protesta, merong trillion march, merong ano-anong march, nakita niyo po ba doon ng vice-presidente? Yes or no lang po?

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: Saan po ang protesta? Sa

turns.speaker: Sen. Robinhood “Robin” Padilla
turns.text: lahat po ng protesta na ganap. Dilawan, Pinklawan, Duterte, ano man po. Wala akong personal knowledge, Sir. Yes or no lang po. Nakita niyo po ba doon si Vice Presidente? Nagsalita po ba siya? Nagbigay po ba siya ng panahon dyan sa mga yan?

turns.speaker: Sen. Robinhood “Robin” Padilla
turns.text: Insofar as I'm concerned, wala akong nakita, Sir. Wala akong nakita. Okay lang po. Maraming salamat po.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Thank you, Sen. Judge Padilla. Atty. Lotoc, you are excused and the court thanks you for your time and cooperation with this impeachment court. Thank

turns.speaker: Atty. Jeremy C. Lotoc
turns.text: you very much, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: May I ask, good, that the Honorable Defensor is standing up. Tomorrow, the subpoena for Atty. Lopez is only for today and tomorrow. The subpoena thus far, yesterday rather, and today. The subpoena for Captain Belio is for... Ah, no subpoena, but she is scheduled to testify tomorrow. So what is your pleasure, Honorable Defensor?

turns.speaker: Rep. Lorenz R. Defensor
turns.text: Your Honors, before we proceed any further, the prosecution respectfully requests for a five-minute recess. Just five minutes, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: You can do your thing, Honorable Defensor, while I recognize Senator Judge... With the permission of Senator Judge Cayetano, of course.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Can they

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: do their thing?

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: I was going to suggest that I have a question about tomorrow. Maybe the defense can do their huddle while I ask this question. The question naman is...

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Sen. Cayetano, Alan is recognized.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Thank you Mr. Presiding Officer, Mr. Senate President. This is addressed actually to the Presiding Officer, Senate President, and our colleagues. So are we going to have the oral arguments tomorrow? Yes. So I think we all received the...

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Copies have been distributed.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: The memoranda of

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: the parties have been

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: distributed. More or less it's 33 and 32 pages. So that's 60 pages. I'm beginning to study it today because I had to study about other matters tomorrow. So the second question is while we will have the oral arguments tomorrow, will we decide as a body tomorrow or we have a little bit more time to digest what was discussed tomorrow and then decide? We will

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: decide as a body tomorrow because my understanding is the parties will be needing time to analyze whatever data will be produced should the subpoenas be granted.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: But that is for Article 2.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: That is correct, Your Honor. That is for Article 2.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Which we will start hearing in August, right?

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: As of now, it is the last one but as we had talked about earlier, the prosecutors can decide to bump it up depending on their strategy to present evidence.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: So I'm not moving that we postpone the oral arguments tomorrow because I think we're ready to listen but I do want to make an intelligent decision and there are many many issues from the test of If it's definite, is it a fishing expedition, 20 years or you know so there's so many issues would it be possible that we also have our own huddle tomorrow before we decide just in case we're not I mean if everyone's ready to decide tomorrow who am I to stop the decision but I just don't want to make a mistake in deciding at medyo makapal tong

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Assuming we read it once tonight, maybe once tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: The presiding officer yields to the senate president with respect to the calling of a caucus tomorrow and what time. Para siya magpakain hindi ako.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Well, let me leave it to the Presiding Officer and Senate President. My proposal is after the oral arguments and after all the senator-judges have asked their questions, just so that we have one more night or one weekend to go through it. If we're not going to vote on it and we have a consensus, then no problem. And there's a precedent because we did this during the time of the late Senate President Enrile when it came to issues of utmost importance that could decide the impeachment-trial results one way or the other. But that does have implications in terms of precedent, especially itong pinag-uusapan natin, AMLA at saka BIR.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: The Senate President is recognized to respond.

turns.speaker: Sen. Sherwin T. Gatchalian
turns.text: I share the same feeling with Senator-Judge Alan Cayetano. I started reading both memos and, indeed, it's quite lengthy and complicated, and we need to also consult our legal teams. So may I propose, Mr. Presiding Officer, to have a caucus tomorrow at 10:00 a.m. so that we can thoroughly discuss this?

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: After the oral arguments.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Senate President, I really thank you that twice already during impeachment, without talking, we have the same wavelength. May I propose that if we have a caucus after the oral arguments, just so that we can—for all we know, maganda iyong discussion and we're enlightened by the prosecution and [unclear]. And, to be honest, I'll probably still be reading this at 10:00 a.m. If that is [unclear], we can have a caucus maybe after—

turns.speaker: Sen. Sherwin T. Gatchalian
turns.text: During the break. After the oral arguments, we'll pause for a break and have a caucus. We can call a longer break, Senator-Judge.

turns.speaker: Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano
turns.text: Thank you, Senate President and Senator.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Is the Honorable Defensor ready after his five-minute huddle?

turns.speaker: Rep. Lorenz R. Defensor
turns.text: Yes, Your Honor. Your Honor, may I request the Court to recognize the counsel for the panel of prosecutors, Atty. Lorna Patajo Capunan, Your Honor.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Atty. Kapunan, counsel for the prosecutors is recognized.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: What do you have for us, ma'am?

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: Magandang gabi po sa inyong lahat, Atty. Lorna Patau Capunan, counsel for the prosecutors under the control and supervision of the House Panel of Prosecutors.

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: If I may, Your Honors.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Please proceed.

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: I can see Sen. Panfilo Lacson coming in, at narinig ko po iyong kaniyang interview noong sinabi po niya na baka magkaapo na tayo dito at magkaroon na ng national bird, eh hindi pa tapos ang impeachment trial.

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: Baca magka-apu na tayo dito at magkaroon na ng national bird, eh

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: hindi pa tapos ang impeachment trial na ito. We have seen, we have seen.

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: This is... Mami

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: said national bird.

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: Hindi po ba, Senator Lacson? Well, somebody who interviewed you said that you said that. It

turns.speaker: Sen. Panfilo M. Lacson
turns.text: must be another... Senator Judge or another person. Talking about birds, okay. Please proceed, ma'am. I never talked about birds.

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: Then definitely my information was hearsay.

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: In any event, in the last four trial days, we have had several hours of legal calisthenics, direct examination,

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: Cross-examination and today we also had redirect and recross. A total of approximately eight hours a day and two witnesses. Today we are supposed to hear a subpoenaed witness, Atty. Zulaica Lopez. And after her, another witness, subpoenaed or Atty.

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: to appear here, Captain Belinda Bello. After hearing the two competent and credible witnesses, not expert witness, but through their credentials, showed that they were competent to testify on the matters that they were asked to authenticate. After evaluating...

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: Belinda Bello

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: Through these two witnesses, 19 documentary evidence from Agent Kalilong and 45 documentary evidence from our recent witness, Atty. Lotoc. And after the very clarificatory and probing questions of our senator judges, After evaluation and not only during this five-minute hurdle, it is the wisdom of the public prosecutors as expressed through this representation that we find it Totally unnecessary, redundant, and a surplusage to still present Atty. Zuleika Lopez and as well, Captain Belinda Bello. Let me just state for the record the reasons why. Had we been able to present Atty. Zuleika Lopez She would have proven three things. Or we would want to have proven three things. First, that she was personally present inside that detention center when the vice president uttered the video Exhibit P-4-10. When she uttered the statements that she had contracted. That she had already contracted a killer. And you have heard this already before. And so on. To

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: kill the President, the First Lady, and the Speaker of the House. That would have been the first offer of testimony: that she was personally present inside that detention center when the Vice President uttered those statements. Admitted already. Admitted by no less than Atty. Vinluan here, who, in his closing remarks or opening remarks, mentioned more than ten times that that press conference occurred, Atty. Zuleika Lopez and the Vice President were there, and that in that press conference or live broadcast, the Vice President did utter the statements we have heard time and again. Exhibit P-4-10. Although Atty. Vinluan says yes ten times—I counted just now—the admission there as to the utterance was made ten times.

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: Atty. Vinluan did say that it is a matter of interpretation. He says that the Vice President did not act as Vice President when she made those utterances. He tried, attempted to give a humane picture

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: picture to the Vice President that she had reacted as mother, sister, brother? No. And that

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: that She was not reacting in her capacity as Vice President. But in that statement that Atty.

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: Bin Luan mentioned, there was admission as to the utterances being made more than ten times, he said. Our interpretation is wrong, but again, that is left to the discretion of this court. So that was the first. The fact that there were utterances made in a press conference and that Atty. Zulweka was president. No need to present Atty. Lopez for this purpose. Secondly, our second purpose was that

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: Atty. Zuleika Lopez was not only present but so were other media personnel. Present there, who heard the utterances of the Vice President. And lastly, we would have offered Atty. Zuleika Lopez to confirm the authenticity and the provenance of that video. Exhibit P-4-10. Totally... Unnecessary because why? Because the defense themselves used the very same video said exhibit in their defense when they showed Atty. Zuleika Lopez crying and allegedly complaining about

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: about... the violation of our human rights so by their own admission there is no question

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: There is no question about this video, so it is our contention, and we hereby manifest that, with these admissions on file. And thank—

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: thank thank you to the senator judges for the clarificatory questions propounded and uh i specifically like

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: To say thank you to Senator Vicente Sotto, for, in his brief statement by virtue of clarification, bringing us back to what this trial is all about. We are not a criminal court, and much time has been spent: is there grave threats? Is there inciting to sedition? All of this is relevant, but in the context of: by doing these grave threats and by inciting to sedition, does it make the Vice President a violator of the Constitution? Does it make her a violator of her solemn oath of office? Is this a high crime? Is this betrayal of public trust? That is what this impeachment is all about. It is not what Atty. Vinluan says. If it is grave threats, by all means, we admit: prisión correccional, six months to six years, and that's a fine of two thousand pesos. If it is sedition, the same. The MTC should be trying these crimes, or the RTC. But

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: But that's not what this is all about.

turns.speaker: Sen. Francis “Chiz” Escudero
turns.text: Atty. Kapunan, with your indulgence, kindly take up the matter of the presentation of witnesses, because that is the subject at hand.

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: Correct. So, going back to why we are making this manifestation,

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: We have said, and I have said on behalf of the public prosecutors, Your Honors, that we will no longer be presenting Atty. Zuleika Lopez. And, Your Honors, in addition, because the testimony of Capt. Belinda Bello is merely corroborative—she would have been presented only to corroborate the fact that there was a transfer order made in the detention center—

turns.speaker: Atty. Lorna Patajo-Kapunan
turns.text: merely corroborative.
